Q: Can you make custom operators in C++? A:

I have created the following two macros:

#define define const struct

#define operator(ReturnType, OperatorName, FirstOperandType, SecondOperandType) \
    OperatorName ## _ {} OperatorName;\
    template <typename T>\
    struct OperatorName ## Proxy {\
        OperatorName ## Proxy(const T& t) : t_(t) {}\
        const T& t_;\
        static ReturnType _ ## OperatorName ## _(const FirstOperandType a, const SecondOperandType b);\
    };\
    template <typename T>\
    inline OperatorName ## Proxy<T> operator<(const T& lhs, const OperatorName ## _& rhs) {\
        return OperatorName ## Proxy<T>(lhs);\
    }\
    inline ReturnType operator>(const OperatorName ## Proxy<FirstOperandType>& lhs, const SecondOperandType& rhs) {\
        return OperatorName ## Proxy<FirstOperandType>::_ ## OperatorName ## _(lhs.t_, rhs);\
    }\
    template <typename T>\
    inline ReturnType OperatorName ## Proxy<T>::_ ## OperatorName ## _(const FirstOperandType a, const SecondOperandType b)

Now, you could define your custom operator as follows:

// The arguments are the return type, the name of the operator, the left operand type and the right operand type, respectively
define operator(bool, myOr, bool, bool) {
    return a || b;
}

// Finally, you may want to define a macro to avoid putting the operator name within angle brackets
#define myOr <myOr>

Usage:

bool a = true myOr false;
// a == true

Warning

While this has been an interesting exercise, it demonstrates how bad it is to have a macro-enabled precompiler. Adding custom operators like this can easily lead to a sort of metalanguage. Despite C++'s bad design, changing it with awkward macros will only make for an even worse language. Use standard C++ (which makes your code understandable by other people) or switch to a different language altogether that suits you better.

SHORTLY: You just shouldn't be using this. Refrain from using macros as much as possible.

Q: Visual Studio Code unable to create java gradle projects A:

The problem is not directly related to vscode or gradle but it was gradle setup problem. Use sdkman for anything related to java. it can install gradle mvn java itself with multiple versions, scala and more. Q: CodeIgniter's select() method containing aliased columns and an SQL function emits a query error A:

Judging by the year this question was posted and the parentheses around the FROM table hints that the installed CodeIgniter is likely to be version 2. I say this because version 3 had several refinements in the query builder pattern which eliminate some previously encountered breakage.

My observations are:

  1. os.group contains mysql keyword group and I don't know if it is being properly identifier quoted. See also Error 1064 at JOIN of table named "groups" in CodeIgniter query
  2. All of the aliases in the SELECT clause are single-quoted which is allowed in MySQL, but for broader validity using identifier quotes (backticks in this case) would be more ideal.
  3. For consistency, country 'Country' should have AS between the column and the alias.
  4. Before CI3, it may have been necessary to pass false as the second parameter of the select() call to explicitly disabled automated escaping/quoting.
  5. The select() line of code is very long so to improve readability, I recommend declaring a re-usable array of columns/aliases instead.
  6. Until you isolate exactly what part of your rendered SELECT clause is broken, you can explicitly disable auto-escaping and manually apply identifier quotes.
protected array $osAliases = [
    'first_name' => 'First Name',
    'last_name' => 'Last Name',
    'phone' => 'Phone',
    'group' => 'Group',
    'gender' => 'Gender',
    'birth_date' => 'DOB',
    'email' => 'Email',
    'street_address' => 'Address',
    'city' => 'City',
    'province' => 'Province',
    'postal_code' => 'Postal Code',
    'country' => 'Country',
    'payment_amount' => 'Payment Amount',
];

public function getOfflineShoppersWithNotes(): array
{
    foreach ($this->osAliases as $col => $alias) {
        $this->db->select(vsprintf(
            '%s AS %s',
            $this->db->escape_identifiers(["os.$col", $alias])
        ), false);
    }
                
    return $this->db
        ->select(vsprintf(
            '%s AS %s',
            $this->db->escape_identifiers(['an.notes', 'Notes'])
        ), false)
        ->select(vsprintf(
            "DATE_FORMAT(%s, '%%d/%%m/%%Y') AS %s",
            $this->db->escape_identifiers(['payment_date', 'Payment Date'])
        ), false)
        ->join('athlete_notes an', 'id');
        ->group_by(['first_name', 'last_name'])
        ->order_by('last_name, first_name')
        ->get('offline_shoppers os')
        ->result_array();
}

Q: Show just CircleCI jobs (not workflow) as GitHub check A:

In your GitHub branch protection rules you can enable/disable the specific CircleCI checks that you want to protect your PRs with. Don't remove the checks orb or uninstall the app as the previous answer recommended as that will remove all of these.
